messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 67 omitted, sha256 a11a3f9ffe5349dd>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The document defines Confidential Information broadly to include written, oral, and physical materials and business topics, not only technical information, so the hypothesis's restriction is contradicted.
<quote check="near">Confidential Information shall mean all information provided by Disclosing Party with respect to the Invention regardless of whether it is written, oral, audio tapes, video tapes, computer discs, machines, prototypes, designs, specifications, articles of manufacture, drawings, human or machine readable documents.</quote>
<quote check="exact">Confidential Information shall also include all information related to the Invention provided by Disclosing Party to Receiving Party prior to the signing of this agreement.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 90
reason: The Invention definition expressly covers business topics, and Confidential Information is defined as all information provided with respect to the Invention, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">shall mean all information relating to products, applications, systems, components, technologies and business topics</quote>
<quote check="exact">“Confidential Information” shall mean all information provided by Disclosing Party with respect to the Invention</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 80
reason: Confidential Information covers all information about the Invention, and the Invention is defined to include business topics, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">shall mean all information relating to products, applications, systems, components, technologies and business topics</quote>
<quote check="exact">“Confidential Information” shall mean all information provided by Disclosing Party with respect to the Invention</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 88, "quotes": ["shall mean all information relating to products, applications, systems, components, technologies and business topics", "“Confidential Information” shall mean all information provided by Disclosing Party with respect to the Invention"], "reason": "Confidential Information covers all information about the Invention, which is defined to include business topics, so it is not limited to technical information."}
